chapter: Brass band style, leadership and recording
title: Wendell Eugene, Tuba Fats and recording the young brass bands
summary: Praise for trombonist Wendell Eugene and Tuba Fats, and recordings of Rebirth, New Birth and other young bands.

blocks.x: I don't know. That's kind of a trombone playing like he does is kind of a dying R.

Oh yeah because it's trombone playing man. He can play. That man can play. I remember a man. And when we were younger. Before he died Mr. Sales was part of my magnificent self. Emmanuel Sales and so forth. Well. Tuba Fats plays.
Tuba Fats still works with you?

Oh yes. Yes. Yes. I worked with Tuba Fats for the past 22 years. He used to run behind us in little sharp pants. In his raggedy horn. We told him one Sunday was having a Mother's Day parade. Go get your horn and come on back. He never got back. He was too scared to come back.
I can't see him as a little anything.
Well he was a little short fat boy. That's what he was.

Yeah. But you know I've recorded the rebirth. The new birth. The young Olympians. The soul rebels. And. The little rascals. All of those. All those young brass band players. You know. We had a chance to. I had a chance to do that.
